title: 4SD0 exam-style questions written for this lesson (lesson 107)
subject: Science (GCSE Biology, Chemistry, Physics)
source: Seeded from gcse-science/y11 lesson 107 (4SD0 exam-style questions written for this lesson (portal question sheet with mark scheme))
intro: Lesson 107: Revision: B3 reproduction in plants. Answer every question. Show your working. Mark it with the mark scheme and log any errors in your repair list.

questions.q: Plan an investigation to show that seeds need water to germinate. Portal response box.
questions.a: Two sets of the same seeds (1), same number and type (1); one with damp cotton wool, one dry (1); same temperature and oxygen/light (1); leave several days (1); count the number germinated and compare / calculate % (1)
questions.model: Teacher writes the first point: 'Place 20 cress seeds on damp cotton wool and 20 on dry cotton wool.'

questions.q: Describe how a pollen grain from one flower leads to a seed in another.
questions.a: Pollen carried by insect/wind to the stigma (1); pollen tube grows down the style (1) to the ovule (1); male nucleus fuses with female nucleus/fertilisation (1)

questions.q: Give one advantage and one disadvantage of cuttings for a farmer.
questions.a: Advantage: quick, identical desired features (1); disadvantage: no variation, all vulnerable to the same disease (1)

questions.q: Explain why offspring from asexual reproduction are identical.
questions.a: Only one parent (1); cells divide by mitosis so genetic material is copied exactly (1)
questions.model: One parent, no fusion of gametes. Mitosis copies DNA exactly. So offspring are genetically identical.

questions.q: State what happens to the ovule and ovary after fertilisation.
questions.a: Ovule becomes the seed (1); ovary becomes the fruit (1)

questions.q: Give two adaptations of wind-pollinated anthers and pollen.
questions.a: Anthers hang outside the flower; pollen is light and produced in large amounts
